summary: CCC-built L-4 cab and wooden tower of 1934-35 on Whitmore Mountain, Colville Reservation; a 53-ft steel live-in tower replaced it in the 1960s and is staffed each summer.

facts.design: 53 ft all-steel live-in tower (built in the 1960s); the historic L-4 cab (1934) stands about a quarter mile away
facts.status_note: The steel tower stands and is staffed each summer. The historic L-4 cab also stands on site, in very poor condition.

access.note: The steel tower is locked and sits on land granted by a private landowner. The register says you can climb the stairs to a viewing platform just below the cab, but no administrator source says whether visitors may use it. Ask the Colville Indian Reservation administrators before visiting.

visit.trail_note: TrailChick describes the site as driveable, with directions that follow BIA Road 67 from Nespelem. The historic L-4 cab is about a quarter mile from the steel tower.

events.note: Work camp on the mountain; lumber hauled up, poles cut and a trail built
L-4 cab built about a quarter mile northeast of the current steel lookout, per the register
Three-legged 60 ft wooden tower with 7x7 ft cab built by CCC; the register gives a reported cost of $1,046 for both structures
Teachers hired as summer fire lookouts in the Colville national forest; Georgia Brown named on Whitmore Mountain
Inspection report calls the wooden tower badly deteriorated and unsafe; proposes a 50 ft steel tower with quarters on top, 1,200 ft south of the old site
Letter suggests moving the new tower a quarter mile southwest, onto privately owned land
Whitmore fire started by lightning on August 3, 2021; crews dug a hand line around the historic L-4 cab and wrapped it; both lookouts survived
Registered April 13, 2022 as US 1565, WA 92; nominated by Christine Estrada

corrections.why: 2.1 m does not match any source. The present steel live-in tower is 53 ft, about 16.2 m.

corrections.proposed: 53 ft all-steel live-in tower; the historic L-4 cab (1934) stands nearby
corrections.why: The L-4 is the historic cab. The lookout in use is the 53 ft steel live-in tower built in the 1960s.

corrections.proposed: 1934-1935 (CCC cab and wooden tower); present steel tower circa the 1960s
corrections.why: The register's 'Built' field for the steel tower reads 'Circa 1960's', and the CCC structures date to 1934-1935. The 1960 date is the year of the inspection report that condemned the wooden tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the 1960 inspection report put the CCC structures in 1934-1935, and a January 1935 newspaper item describes CCC crews working on the lookout station. Firelookout.com and a TrailChick photo caption date the wooden tower and cab to 1938. The story uses 1934-1935 and notes the 1938 dating.

The 1960 inspection report proposed a site 1,200 ft south of the old tower, and a 1962 letter suggested a site a quarter mile southwest. The register places the historic L-4 cab a quarter mile northeast of the steel tower. The story does not give the exact site of the new tower.

The register says a stair leads up to a viewing platform below the cab. The register also says the lookout is locked and the site sits on land granted by a private landowner. The story treats access as permission-only and says visitors should ask first.

notes_for_editor: Early dates conflict: 1934-35 for the CCC cab and wooden tower (register, 1960 inspection report, 1935 newspaper item) versus 1938 (Firelookout.com, TrailChick photo caption). The steel tower is dated only to 'circa the 1960s' by the register; the exact year was not found, so no event year is given for it. The brief's 1960 built date and 2.1 m height are both wrong per these sources. The Colville Reservation status (administration, permission from a private landowner) is taken from the register. Access is permission-only in the record; the register's stair-to-platform note is reported but not endorsed. The 2024 staffing as_of comes from TrailChick's page (last updated March 24, 2024).
